## How to Sign

### Option 1: CLA Assistant (Automated)

If your organization is making a Pull Request to our GitHub repository, the CLA Assistant bot will automatically detect that a Corporate CLA is required. An authorized representative of your organization can sign through the CLA Assistant interface.

### Option 2: Manual Signing

If you prefer to sign manually, please:

1. Fork this repository
2. Create a file in `.github/cla-signatures/corporate/` named `<organization-name>.md`
3. Copy the following content into the file:

```markdown
# Corporate CLA Signature

- **Corporation Name**: [Legal Name of Corporation]
- **Corporation Address**: [Full Address]
- **Primary Contact Name**: [Contact Person Name]
- **Primary Contact Email**: [Contact Email]
- **GitHub Organization**: [GitHub Organization Name, if applicable]
- **Date**: [Date of Signature]
- **Authorized Signatory**: [Name and Title of Person Signing]

## Authorization

I am authorized to sign this Agreement on behalf of the Corporation named above.

## Employee/Contractor Authorization

The following individuals are authorized to Submit Contributions on behalf of the Corporation:

- [GitHub Username 1]
- [GitHub Username 2]
- [Add more as needed]

## Signature

I agree to the terms of the OpenBrowser Corporate Contributor License Agreement on behalf of the Corporation named above.

Signed: [Authorized Signatory Name]
Title: [Title]
Date: [Date]
```

4. Commit this file with message: `docs: sign corporate CLA for [Corporation Name]`
5. Submit a Pull Request

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Do we need a Corporate CLA if only one employee is contributing?**
A: Yes, if the contributions are made as part of the employee's work for the Corporation, a Corporate CLA is required.

**Q: Can we add more authorized contributors later?**
A: Yes, you can update the list of authorized contributors by submitting a Pull Request that modifies your signature file.

**Q: Do we need to sign both Individual and Corporate CLA?**
A: No. Corporate CLA covers all contributions made by authorized employees and contractors. Individual contributors who are not contributing on behalf of an employer should sign the Individual CLA.
